why: Every alternative origin is ruled out deterministically. No production path can generate 100%: normalize.ts passes PERCENT through verbatim with no default or scaling, the wire schema makes numeric fields optional, UNLIMITED_CAPACITY exists for exactly this uncapped shape, and the prompt and few-shots contain no 100%. The value is absent from the anchor and from all nine context items - the bare token '100' appears nowhere in the candidate's evidence. What remains is an assertion the model produced, which nothing downstream examined.
confidence: HIGH on the elimination of deterministic origins; MEDIUM on the model-origin attribution itself, because the raw response was not persisted and cannot be quoted. I am not claiming to have seen the model emit it.

secondaryRootCauses.detail: The numeric-grounding gate (reconciliation.ts findIrOnlyNumericItems) inventories only structured AMOUNT | PERCENT | RATIO nodes. A number in a free-text field is never inventoried, so it is never reconciled. Proven by probe: the prose shape produces no IR_ONLY finding.

Sufficiency is declared per RULE, not per numeric field. 7.2(f)'s rule reported sufficiency COMPLETE while the unit was REVIEW_REQUIRED for two unrelated reasons, so nothing in the record says 'this number is ungrounded'.

My own validation runner persisted only summary fields, discarding rawModelOutput and the tool log that the compiler result already carried. That is why the first stage cannot be pinned. A one-line change to the runner would have settled this mission definitively.

notTheCause: NORMALIZER_INVENTED_VALUE - no such transform exists on the compile path
PROMPT_SCHEMA_FORCED_VALUE - numeric fields are optional and UNLIMITED_CAPACITY is available
NOT_ACTUALLY_UNSUPPORTED - the token '100' is absent from every channel
the candidate-span defect - 7.2(f) is single-key, its operative text was byte-identical before and after R1, and it has no linked parent

remediationOptions.name: Numeric-bearing IR fields require source-backed evidence or are nulled / marked unresolved
remediationOptions.falseCreditProtection: HIGHEST - an ungrounded number cannot survive in the IR at all.
remediationOptions.falseNegativeRisk: HIGH - a legitimate value drawn from an authenticated definition or cross-reference would be destroyed unless the evidence check covers every retrieval channel, which is exactly where 7.1(d)'s $800,000,000 lives. Nulling loses information a reviewer needs.
remediationOptions.downstreamImpact: Large - changes IR shape and what the runtime sees.
remediationOptions.provenance: Requires per-value provenance to know which channel supported it.

remediationOptions.name: Verifier explicitly reconciles every material numeric assertion, including prose, against operative + authenticated context
remediationOptions.falseCreditProtection: HIGH - closes the measured gap: prose numerics become visible to reconciliation.
remediationOptions.falseNegativeRisk: LOW-MEDIUM - risk is noise, not loss: prose numbers legitimately restating a supported value would need matching. Review volume rises.
remediationOptions.downstreamImpact: None - verification-side only, no IR shape change.
remediationOptions.complexity: MEDIUM - extend the IR inventory to scan free-text fields and route hits through findIrOnlyNumericItems.

remediationOptions.name: Compiler schema permits explicit UNKNOWN / null rather than forcing numeric completion
remediationOptions.falseCreditProtection: LOW here - the schema ALREADY permits this. Numeric wire fields are optional and UNLIMITED_CAPACITY exists. Nothing forced the value.
remediationOptions.complexity: n/a - measured as already satisfied; listed only to record that it is not the fix.

remediationOptions.name: An unsupported numeric forces rule-level REVIEW_REQUIRED and blocks executable downstream use
remediationOptions.falseCreditProtection: MEDIUM on its own, HIGH combined with B - B detects, D contains.
remediationOptions.falseNegativeRisk: LOW - it gates rather than deletes, so nothing is lost.
remediationOptions.downstreamImpact: Significant and independently valuable: the Phase-4 runtime currently has ZERO references to sufficiency or verification state, so today an ungrounded structured number would evaluate as a normal executable value. D is the only option that closes that.
remediationOptions.provenance: Needs a per-rule grounding flag the runtime can read.
remediationOptions.complexity: MEDIUM-HIGH - touches the Phase-4 boundary, which is frozen in this programme.

recommendedFix: B first, then D. B is verification-side only, closes the measured gap (prose numerics invisible to reconciliation), changes no IR shape and carries the lowest false-negative risk. D is the larger and more important finding - REVIEW_REQUIRED does not currently stop anything downstream - but it touches the Phase-4 boundary and deserves its own mission rather than being folded into a numeric-grounding fix. A is rejected: nulling would destroy legitimately context-supported values like 7.1(d)'s. C is already satisfied.
falseCreditRiskOfRecommendedFix: LOW. B only adds detections; it cannot create credit. It reduces the chance an ungrounded number is presented as a populated term.
falseNegativeRiskOfRecommendedFix: LOW-MEDIUM. B may raise review volume by flagging prose numbers that merely restate a supported value; mitigated by matching prose hits against the same authenticated-evidence set the structured path already uses, so a value present in an authenticated definition is not re-flagged.
